latin: Vesper adest: iuvenes, consurgite: vesper Olympo
english: Vesper is here: youths, rise up together: Vesper from Olympus
note: Speaker: Youths (Merrill's head). Vesper = the evening star. Olympo: ablative, "from (or on) Olympus", i.e. the sky.

latin: exspectata diu vix tandem lumina tollit.
english: long awaited, scarcely at last raises his lights.
note: lumina: "lights", i.e. its light (the word can also mean "eyes").

latin: surgere iam tempus, iam pinguis linquere mensas;
english: now it is time to rise, now to leave the fat tables;
note: pinguis = pingues (acc. pl.), lit. "fat": i.e. richly laden tables.

latin: iam veniet virgo, iam dicetur hymenaeus.
english: now will come the maiden, now will be said the hymenaeus.
note: hymenaeus = the wedding song; dicetur lit. "will be said", i.e. sung.

latin: Hymen O Hymenaee, Hymen ades O Hymenaee.
english: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen, be present, O Hymenaeus.
note: Refrain; Hymenaee is vocative of Hymenaeus, the wedding god. Rendered identically each time.

latin: cernitis, innuptae, iuvenes? consurgite contra:
english: do you see, unmarried girls, the youths? Rise up together in answer:
note: Speaker: Maidens. contra: "opposite, in turn", i.e. to match them.

latin: nimirum Oetaeos ostendit Noctifer ignes.
english: doubtless the Night-bringer shows the Oetaean fires.
note: Noctifer = the evening star; the "Oetaean fires" are its light rising over Mount Oeta (associated with Hesperus).

latin: sic certe est: viden ut perniciter exsiluere?
english: So surely it is: do you see how swiftly they have leapt out?
note: viden = videsne.

latin: non temere exsiluere; canent quod vincere par est.
english: not at random have they leapt out; they will sing what it is fitting to overcome.
note: par est: "it is fitting/proper"; i.e. a song worth defeating (that the girls must outdo).

latin: Hymen O Hymenaee, Hymen ades O Hymenaee.
english: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen, be present, O Hymenaeus.

latin: non facilis nobis, aequales, palma parata est:
english: not easy for us, age-mates, has the palm been prepared:
note: Speaker: Youths. palma = the palm of victory, i.e. the prize. aequales: companions of the same age.

latin: adspicite, innuptae secum ut meditata requirunt.
english: look, how the unmarried girls within themselves seek again things rehearsed.
note: meditata requirunt: they recall what they have practised.

latin: non frustra meditantur; habent memorabile quod sit.
english: not in vain do they rehearse; they have what may be memorable.

latin: nec mirum, penitus quae tota mente laborant.
english: nor is it a wonder, they who deep within with the whole mind labour.
note: quae: feminine plural, the girls ("since they ...").

latin: nos alio mentes, alio divisimus aures:
english: we our minds to one place, to another have divided our ears:
note: i.e. our minds were on other things than what we heard.

latin: iure igitur vincemur; amat victoria curam.
english: rightly therefore we shall be conquered; victory loves care.

latin: quare nunc animos saltem convertite vestros:
english: therefore now at least turn your minds:

latin: dicere iam incipient, iam respondere decebit.
english: now they will begin to speak, now it will be fitting to respond.

latin: Hymen o Hymenaee, Hymen ades o Hymenaee.
english: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen, be present, O Hymenaeus.
note: Source prints "o" lowercase from here; same refrain.

latin: Hespere, qui caelo fertur crudelior ignis?
english: Hesperus, what more cruel fire is borne in the sky?
note: Speaker: Maidens. Hespere: vocative of Hesperus, the evening star. qui: interrogative adjective with ignis.

latin: qui natam possis complexu avellere matris,
english: you who could tear away a daughter from the embrace of her mother,
note: qui (masc. sing.) refers to Hesperus, with second-person possis.

latin: complexu matris retinentem avellere natam
english: from the embrace of her mother tear away the clinging daughter
note: retinentem: "holding on", i.e. clinging to her mother.

latin: et iuveni ardenti castam donare puellam.
english: and to a burning young man give the chaste girl.
note: ardenti: "burning", i.e. with desire.

latin: quid faciunt hostes capta crudelius urbe?
english: what do enemies do more cruel when a city has been captured?
note: capta urbe: ablative absolute.

latin: Hymen o Hymenaee, Hymen ades o Hymenaee.
english: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen, be present, O Hymenaeus.

latin: Hespere, qui caelo lucet iucundior ignis?
english: Hesperus, what more pleasant fire shines in the sky?
note: Speaker: Youths.

latin: qui desponsa tua firmes conubia flammma,
english: you who could make firm with your flame the promised marriages,
note: Source spells "flammma" (sic, for flamma); kept as printed. qui (masc. sing.) = Hesperus.

latin: quae pepigere viri, pepigerunt ante parentes,
english: which the men have pledged, have pledged beforehand the parents,
note: quae: neuter plural, the marriages. viri: "men", i.e. the bridegrooms.

latin: nec iunxere prius quam se tuus extulit ardor.
english: and did not join before your burning raised itself.
note: ardor: "burning", i.e. the star's blaze.

latin: quid datur a divis felici optatius hora?
english: what is given by the gods more longed-for than the happy hour?
note: felici hora: ablative of comparison.

latin: Hymen o Hymenaee, Hymen ades o Hymenaee.
english: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen, be present, O Hymenaeus.

latin: Hesperus e nobis, aequales, abstulit unam
english: Hesperus from us, age-mates, has taken away one
note: Speaker: Maidens. The sentence is broken off by the gap that follows.
Gap marker kept from the source (lines lost): the rest of the maidens' complaint and the start of the youths' reply are missing.

latin: namque tuo adventu vigilat custodia semper.
english: for at your coming the watch always keeps awake.
note: Speaker: Youths (resuming after the gap).

latin: nocte latent fures, quos idem saepe revertens,
english: at night thieves lie hidden, whom you, the same, often returning,
note: idem: masc. sing., Hesperus; quos: masc. pl., the thieves.

latin: Hespere, mutato comprendis nomine eosdem.
english: Hesperus, with changed name catch, the same ones.
note: i.e. returning as the morning star (Eous) under another name. comprendis = comprehendis.

latin: at libet innuptis ficto te carpere questu.
english: but it pleases the unmarried girls with a feigned complaint to pluck at you.
note: carpere: lit. "to pluck", i.e. to carp at, find fault with.

latin: quid tum, si carpunt tacita quem mente requirunt?
english: what then, if they pluck at him whom with silent mind they seek?
note: quem: masc. sing.; him = Hesperus (or the bridegroom he brings).

latin: Hymen o Hymenaee, Hymen ades o Hymenaee.
english: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen, be present, O Hymenaeus.

latin: ut flos in saeptis secretus nascitur hortis,
english: as a flower in fenced gardens is born set apart,
note: Speaker: Maidens.

latin: ignotus pecori, nullo convulsus aratro,
english: unknown to the flock, by no plough torn up,

latin: quem mulcent aurae, firmat sol, educat imber,
english: which the breezes caress, the sun strengthens, the rain brings up,
note: quem: masc. sing., the flower (flos).

latin: multi illum pueri, multae optavere puellae;
english: many boys it, many girls have longed for;

latin: idem cum tenui carptus defloruit ungui,
english: the same, when plucked by a thin fingernail, has shed its bloom,

latin: nulli illum pueri, nullae optavere puellae:
english: no boys it, no girls have longed for:

latin: sic virgo, dum intacta manet, dum cara suis est;
english: so a maiden, while she remains untouched, while she is dear to her own;
note: suis: "to her own", i.e. her family. The main clause is left elliptical.

latin: cum castum amisit polluto corpore florem,
english: when she has lost her chaste flower, her body having been polluted,
note: flos = her virginity; polluto corpore: ablative absolute.

latin: nec pueris iucunda manet nec cara puellis.
english: neither to boys pleasant does she remain nor dear to girls.

latin: Hymen o Hymenaee, Hymen ades o Hymenaee.
english: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen, be present, O Hymenaeus.

latin: ut vidua in nudo vitis quae nascitur arvo
english: as a widowed vine which is born in a bare field
note: Speaker: Youths. vidua: "widowed", i.e. unmarried to a supporting tree (vines were "wedded" to elms). quae: fem. sing., the vine.

latin: nunquam se extollit, nunquam mitem educat uvam,
english: never raises itself, never brings up a mellow grape,

latin: sed tenerum prono deflectens pondere corpus
english: but bending its tender body with downward weight

latin: iam iam contingit summum radice flagellum,
english: now, now touches the topmost shoot with its root,
note: flagellum: lit. "little whip", a vine shoot; i.e. it droops so low that its tip reaches its root.

latin: hanc nulli agricolae, nulli accoluere iuvenci;
english: her no farmers, no bullocks have tended;
note: hanc: fem., the vine, personified as a woman (so "her"). accoluere: lit. "have dwelt by", i.e. tended.

latin: at si forte eadem est ulmo coniuncta marito,
english: but if by chance the same has been joined to an elm as husband,
note: marito: the elm as "husband" of the vine (literal metaphor).

latin: multi illam agricolae, multi accoluere iuvenci:
english: many farmers her, many bullocks have tended:

latin: sic virgo, dum intacta manet, dum inculta senescit;
english: so a maiden, while she remains untouched, while she grows old untended;
note: inculta: "uncultivated", continuing the vine image.

latin: cum par conubium maturo tempore adepta est,
english: when a matched marriage at the ripe time she has obtained,
note: par conubium: a marriage equal to her.

latin: cara viro magis et minus est invisa parenti.
english: dearer to her husband she is and less hated by her parent.

latin: et tu ne pugna cum tali coniuge, virgo.
english: And you, do not fight with such a spouse, maiden.
note: Speaker: Youths and Maidens (Merrill's head; many editors give these lines to the youths).

latin: non aequum est pugnare, pater cui tradidit ipse,
english: it is not fair to fight him to whom your father himself has handed you,
note: cui: masc. sing., the bridegroom.

latin: ipse pater cum matre, quibus parere necesse est.
english: father himself with mother, whom it is necessary to obey.
note: quibus: plural, the two parents.

latin: virginitas non tota tua est, ex parte parentum est:
english: virginity is not wholly yours, in part it is the parents':

latin: tertia pars patri, pars est data tertia matri,
english: a third part to the father, a part has been given third to the mother,

latin: tertia sola tua est.noli pugnare duobus,
english: a third alone is yours. do not fight two,
note: Source prints "est.noli" without a space; kept as printed. noli pugnare: "do not (be willing to) fight".

latin: qui genero sua iura simul cum dote dederunt.
english: who to the son-in-law have given their rights together with the dowry.
note: qui: masc. pl., the parents.

latin: Hymen o Hymenaee, Hymen ades o Hymenaee.
english: Hymen O Hymenaeus, Hymen, be present, O Hymenaeus.

latin: Super alta vectus Attis celeri rate maria
english: Carried over deep seas, Attis, in a swift craft,
note: vectus: masculine; Attis is grammatically male until the castration.

latin: Phrygium ut nemus citato cupide pede tetigit
english: when the Phrygian grove with hurried foot eagerly he touched

latin: adiitque opaca silvis redimita loca deae,
english: and approached the places of the goddess, shady, wreathed with woods,
note: deae = Cybele.

latin: stimulatus ibi furenti rabie, vagus animis
english: goaded there by raging madness, wandering in his wits,
note: stimulatus, vagus: masculine. animis: plural, "in spirits/mind".

latin: devolvit ili acuto sibi pondera silice.
english: he cast down from himself the weights of his groin with a sharp flint.
note: The self-castration: pondera ili, lit. "the weights of the groin" = his testicles. ili: genitive of ilium/ileum ("groin"). devolvit: "rolled down, cut away".

latin: itaque ut relicta sensit sibi membra sine viro,
english: and so, when he felt his limbs left without the man,
note: sine viro: "without the man", i.e. without manhood. No gendered form in this line; "he" kept until the first feminine form.

latin: etiam recente terrae sola sanguine maculans
english: still with fresh blood staining the soil of the earth,
note: sola: plural, "soils, ground".

latin: niveis citata cepit manibus leve typanum,
english: roused, she seized in snowy hands the light typanum,
note: First shift of grammatical gender: citata is feminine, so Attis is "she" from here wherever the Latin is feminine. typanum (sic, = tympanum): a hand-drum or tambourine.

latin: typanum, tubam Cybelles, tua, mater, initia,
english: the typanum, the trumpet of Cybelle, your mysteries, mother,
note: tubam: lit. "trumpet", i.e. the drum as the call of Cybelle. initia: initiation rites. mater = Cybele, addressed.

latin: quatiensque terga tauri teneris cava digitis
english: and shaking the hollow backs of a bull with tender fingers
note: terga tauri: the bull's hide stretched over the drum.

latin: canere haec suis adorta est tremebunda comitibus
english: began to sing these things to her companions, trembling:
note: adorta est, tremebunda: feminine.

latin: agite ite ad alta, Gallae, Cybeles nemora simul,
english: Come, go to the high groves of Cybele, Gallae, together,
note: No quotation marks added (none in the source). Gallae: feminine form of Galli, the eunuch priests of Cybele. Cybeles: Greek genitive.

latin: simul ite, Dindymenae dominae vaga pecora,
english: together go, wandering herds of the Dindymenian mistress,
note: Dindymene: Cybele, from Mount Dindymus.

latin: aliena quae petentes velut exsules loca
english: who, seeking foreign places like exiles,
note: quae: neuter plural, agreeing with pecora ("herds").

latin: sectam meam exsecutae duce me mihi comites
english: having followed my sect, with me as leader, companions to me,
note: exsecutae: feminine plural (the Gallae).

latin: rapidum salum tulistis truculentaque pelagi
english: have endured the rapid salt sea and the savagery of the ocean
note: truculenta pelagi: lit. "the savage (things) of the sea".

latin: et corpus evirastis Veneris nimio odio,
english: and have unmanned your body from excessive hatred of Venus,
note: evirastis = eviravistis, "you castrated". corpus: singular. Veneris odio: hatred of sexual love.

latin: hilarate erae citatis erroribus animum.
english: gladden the mind of your mistress with hurried wanderings.
note: erae: "mistress", Cybele.

latin: mora tarda mente cedat; simul ite, sequimini
english: let slow delay yield from your mind; together go, follow

latin: Phrygiam ad domum Cybelles, Phrygia ad nemora deae,
english: to the Phrygian home of Cybelle, to the Phrygian groves of the goddess,

latin: ubi cymbalum sonat vox, ubi tympana reboant,
english: where the voice of cymbals sounds, where the tympana re-echo,
note: cymbalum: genitive plural (= cymbalorum).

latin: tibicen ubi canit Phryx curvo grave calamo,
english: where the Phrygian piper sings deep on the curved reed,
note: grave: adverbial, "deeply, low".

latin: ubi capita maenades vi iaciunt hederigerae,
english: where ivy-bearing maenads toss their heads with force,

latin: ubi sacra sancta acutis ululatibus agitant,
english: where they drive on the holy rites with sharp howlings,
note: agitant: "drive, stir up", i.e. celebrate.

latin: ubi suevit illa divae volitare vaga cohors,
english: where that wandering cohort of the goddess is accustomed to flit about,
note: suevit: perfect of suesco, "has become wont".

latin: quo nos decet citatis celerare tripudiis.
english: whither it befits us to hasten with hurried triple-step dances.
note: tripudium: a ritual dance in triple time.

latin: simul haec comitibus Attis cecinit notha mulier,
english: As soon as Attis, a counterfeit woman, sang these things to her companions,
note: notha mulier: lit. "bastard woman", i.e. not a true woman.

latin: thiasus repente linguis trepidantibus ululat,
english: the thiasus suddenly with quivering tongues howls,
note: thiasus: a band of revellers in a cult.

latin: leve tympanum remugit, cava cymbala recrepant,
english: the light tympanum bellows back, the hollow cymbals clash back,

latin: viridem citus adit Idam properante pede chorus.
english: to green Ida swiftly goes the chorus with hastening foot.

latin: furibunda simul anhelans vaga vadit animam agens
english: frenzied, at once panting, wandering, she goes, driving out her breath,
note: furibunda: feminine. animam agens: lit. "driving the breath", i.e. gasping (also used of the dying).

latin: comitata tympano Attis per opaca nemora dux,
english: accompanied by the tympanum, Attis, through the shady groves, leader,
note: comitata: feminine.

latin: veluti iuvenca vitans onus indomita iugi:
english: like a heifer avoiding the burden of the yoke, untamed:
note: indomita: feminine, with iuvenca.

latin: rapidae ducem secuntur Gallae properipedem.
english: swift, the Gallae follow their swift-footed leader.

latin: itaque, ut domum Cybelles tetigere lassulae,
english: and so, when they touched the home of Cybelle, tired out,
note: lassulae: feminine plural diminutive, "little weary ones".

latin: nimio e labore somnum capiunt sine Cerere.
english: from excessive toil they take sleep without Ceres.
note: sine Cerere: "without Ceres", i.e. without food (bread).

latin: piger his labante langore oculos sopor operit:
english: for them sluggish sleep with sinking languor covers the eyes:

latin: abit in quiete molli rabidus furor animi.
english: departs in soft rest the raving fury of the mind.

latin: sed ubi oris aurei Sol radiantibus oculis
english: But when the Sun of golden face with radiant eyes

latin: lustravit aethera album, sola dura, mare ferum,
english: surveyed the white aether, the hard soils, the wild sea,

latin: pepulitque noctis umbras vegetis sonipedibus,
english: and drove out the shadows of night with lively sound-footed steeds,
note: sonipedibus: "sound-foot" horses, the Sun's team.

latin: ibi Somnus excitam Attin fugiens citus abiit:
english: then Sleep, fleeing roused Attis, swiftly went away:
note: excitam: feminine accusative; Attin: Greek accusative.

latin: trepidante eum recepit dea Pasithea sinu.
english: him the goddess Pasithea received in her trembling bosom.
note: eum: masculine, Sleep (Somnus); Pasithea is his wife.

latin: ita de quiete molli rapida sine rabie
english: thus from soft rest, without rapid frenzy,

latin: simul ipsa pectore Attis sua facta recoluit,
english: as soon as Attis herself in her breast reviewed her deeds,
note: ipsa: feminine.

latin: liquidaque mente vidit sine quis ubique foret,
english: and with clear mind saw without what and where she was,
note: sine quis = sine quibus: what she was now without (her manhood, her home) and where she was.

latin: animo aestuante rusum reditum ad vada tetulit.
english: with seething spirit again she bore her return to the shallows.
note: rusum = rursum; tetulit = tulit.

latin: ibi maria vasta visens lacrimantibus oculis
english: there, gazing at the vast seas with weeping eyes,

latin: patriam adlocuta maesta est ita voce miseriter:
english: she, sad, addressed her fatherland thus with voice piteously:
note: adlocuta maesta est: feminine. No quotation marks added.

latin: patria o mei creatrix, patria o mea genetrix,
english: O fatherland, creatress of me, O fatherland, my mother,

latin: ego quam miser relinquens, dominos ut erifugae
english: whom I, wretched, leaving, as from their masters runaway
note: miser: masculine here, though Attis is elsewhere feminine. erifugae: "master-fleeing".

latin: famuli solent, ad Idae tetuli nemora pedem,
english: servants are wont, to the groves of Ida have carried my foot,

latin: ut apud nivem et ferarum gelida stabula forem
english: that among the snow and the frozen lairs of beasts I might be

latin: et earum omnia adirem furibunda latibula,
english: and might approach all their hiding-places, frenzied,
note: furibunda: feminine. earum: feminine plural, of the beasts.

latin: ubinam aut quibus locis te positam, patria, reor?
english: where then or in what places do I think you set, fatherland?

latin: cupit ipsa pupula ad te sibi derigere aciem,
english: the pupil itself longs to direct its gaze toward you,
note: pupula: "little pupil" of the eye.

latin: rabie fera carens dum breve tempus animus est.
english: while for a brief time my mind is free of wild madness.

latin: egone a mea remota haec ferar in nemora domo?
english: Shall I, far removed from my home, be carried into these groves?
note: remota: feminine.

latin: patria, bonis, amicis, genitoribus abero?
english: from fatherland, goods, friends, parents shall I be absent?

latin: abero foro, palaestra, stadio, et gymnasiis?
english: shall I be absent from forum, palaestra, stadium, and gymnasia?

latin: miser ah miser, querendum est etiam atque etiam, anime.
english: wretched, ah wretched, it must be lamented again and again, my soul.
note: miser: masculine, agreeing with anime (vocative, "soul").

latin: quod enim genus figurae est ego non quod obierim?
english: For what kind of shape is there that I have not undergone?

latin: ego mulier, ego adulescens, ego ephebus, ego puer,
english: I a woman, I a young man, I an ephebe, I a boy,
note: The stages run backward from the present: now woman, earlier youth, ephebe, boy. mulier is the reading of the source.

latin: ego gymnasi fui flos, ego eram decus olei:
english: I was the flower of the gymnasium, I was the glory of the oil:
note: olei: the athletes' oil, i.e. the wrestling-ground.

latin: mihi ianuae frequentes, mihi limina tepida,
english: for me the doors were crowded, for me the thresholds warm,
note: i.e. admirers thronged his door.

latin: mihi floridis corollis redimita domus erat,
english: for me with flowery garlands the house was wreathed,

latin: linquendum ubi esset orto mihi sole cubiculum.
english: when the bedchamber had to be left by me, the sun having risen.

latin: ego nunc deum ministra et Cybeles famula ferar?
english: Shall I now be called the servant of the gods and the slave-girl of Cybele?
note: ministra, famula: feminine. deum = deorum. ferar: "be said/called".

latin: ego maenas, ego mei pars, ego vir sterilis ero?
english: I a maenad, I a part of me, I a sterile man shall be?
note: vir sterilis: masculine noun; mei pars: "a part of myself", i.e. mutilated.

latin: ego viridis algida Idae nive amicta loca colam?
english: Shall I inhabit the chilly places of green Ida, clothed in snow?

latin: ego vitam agam sub altis Phrygiae columinibus,
english: Shall I spend life under the lofty summits of Phrygia,
note: columinibus = culminibus.

latin: ubi cerva silvicultrix, ubi aper nemorivagus?
english: where the forest-dwelling hind, where the grove-wandering boar?
note: No verb in the Latin.

latin: iam iam dolet quod egi, iam iamque paenitet.
english: now, now it pains me what I have done, now, now it repents me.
note: dolet, paenitet: impersonal verbs; "me" supplied.

latin: roseis ut huic labellis sonitus citus abiit
english: As from her rosy lips the swift sound went away,
note: huic: feminine dative, Attis.

latin: geminas deorum ad aures nova nuntia referens,
english: bearing new tidings to the twin ears of the gods,

latin: ibi iuncta iuga resoluens Cybele leonibus
english: then Cybele, loosening the yokes joined to the lions,
note: iuga: plural.

latin: laevumque pecoris hostem stimulans ita loquitur.
english: and goading the left-hand enemy of the flock, thus speaks:
note: laevum pecoris hostem: the lion on the left (the near one); "enemy of the flock" = lion.

latin: Agedum, inquit, age ferox i, fac ut hunc furor agitet,
english: Come, she says, come, fierce one, go, make frenzy drive this one,
note: No quotation marks added. hunc: masculine, Cybele speaks of Attis as male.

latin: fac uti furoris ictu reditum in nemora ferat,
english: make that by the stroke of frenzy he carries his return into the groves,

latin: mea libere nimis qui fugere imperia cupit.
english: who too freely desires to flee my commands.
note: qui: masculine singular, Attis.

latin: age caede terga cauda, tua verbera patere,
english: Come, strike your back with your tail, endure your own lashes,

latin: fac cuncta mugienti fremitu loca retonent,
english: make all places re-thunder with bellowing roar,

latin: rutilam ferox torosa cervice quate iubam.
english: fierce, on your muscular neck shake your tawny mane.

latin: ait haec minax Cybelle religatque iuga manu.
english: Thus speaks threatening Cybelle and ties back the yoke with her hand.
note: religat: lit. "ties back"; here usually taken as "unfastens" the lion from the yoke. iuga: plural.

latin: ferus ipse sese adhortans rabidum incitat animo,
english: The wild one himself, urging himself on, rouses himself raging in his spirit,
note: ferus: the lion. rabidum: masculine, predicative.

latin: vadit, fremit, refringit virgulta pede vago.
english: he goes, he roars, he breaks the thickets with wandering foot.

latin: at ubi umida albicantis loca litoris adiit
english: But when he approached the wet places of the whitening shore

latin: tenerumque vidit Attin prope marmora pelagi,
english: and saw tender Attis near the marble expanses of the sea,
note: marmora pelagi: "the marbles of the sea", i.e. its gleaming surface.

latin: facit impetum: ille demens fugit in nemora fera:
english: he makes an attack: that one, mad, flees into the wild groves:
note: ille: masculine, referring to Attis (some editors read illa).

latin: ibi semper omne vitae spatium famula fuit.
english: there always, the whole span of life, she was a slave-girl.
note: famula: feminine.

latin: dea magna, dea Cybelle, dea domina Dindymi,
english: Great goddess, goddess Cybelle, goddess, mistress of Dindymus,

latin: procul a mea tuus sit furor omnis, era, domo:
english: far from my house be all your frenzy, mistress:
note: sit: jussive subjunctive, "may it be". era: "mistress", Cybele.

latin: alios age incitatos, alios age rabidos.
english: others drive roused, others drive raving.
note: alios: masculine plural.
